# Browser targets for the client bundle (SWC syntax lowering, Lightning CSS and
# autoprefixer all read this file).
#
# Next.js 16 raised its built-in default from Next 15's
# `chrome 64, edge 79, firefox 67, opera 51, safari 12` to "baseline widely
# available" -- `chrome 111, edge 111, firefox 111, safari 16.4`. That silently
# drops everything older than iOS 16.4 / Safari 16.4 (March 2023), which is a
# real slice of the traffic for a tool people open on whatever phone they have.
#
# So we keep Next 15's list explicitly. Next only falls back to its own default
# when no browserslist config resolves, so this file is what restores it.
#
# It is also what makes `transpilePackages: ["pdfjs-dist"]` in `next.config.mjs`
# do anything: that entry exists to lower pdf.js's ES2022 syntax for older
# Safari, and under the Next 16 default targets there was nothing left to lower.
#
# Caveat: this only lowers *syntax*. Missing built-ins (`Object.hasOwn`,
# `Array.prototype.at`, `structuredClone`, ...) are not polyfilled -- exactly as
# in Next 15. If we ever need those, add
# `experimental.swcEnvOptions: { mode: "usage", coreJs: "3.x" }`.

chrome 64
